cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in a Command ('Command Injection')

exact_cwe_mechanism.evidence: The code constructs a shell command by substituting user-controlled href into a path template containing %u placeholder, then executes via os.execv("/bin/sh", ["/bin/sh", "-c", path]). This directly matches CWE-77's mechanism of command construction with external input.

connection.evidence: href comes from user-supplied URLs in _goto/_fetch or temporary file paths in _edit. The path template comes from editor configuration or browser configuration. Both flow directly to the shell command execution at line 145.

diff_causality.evidence: This line is the critical substitution that inserts external input into the command template. Without this line, href would not be incorporated into the executed command, preventing the injection vector.

security_control.evidence: Required control: proper neutralization of special shell characters in external input before command construction. Control requirement evidence: shell command execution requires escaping/quoting of metacharacters to prevent injection. Existing controls checked: encoder() function applied after substitution but purpose unclear, no shell escaping or parameterization observed. Deficiency evidence: direct string substitution without shell escaping or parameterization allows injection of command separators.
security_control.required_control: shell escaping or parameterization of external input
security_control.control_requirement_evidence: Shell command execution with external input requires proper escaping to prevent injection of metacharacters like ;, &, |, $, etc.
existing_controls_checked: encoder() function applied after substitution but purpose unclear from evidence
security_control.deficiency_evidence: Direct string substitution without shell escaping or parameterization allows injection of command separators and metacharacters

concrete_impact.evidence: Arbitrary command execution is possible if attacker controls href value and can inject shell metacharacters. The evidence shows direct path to shell execution but doesn't demonstrate specific exploit scenarios.

diff_counterfactual: If the candidate line were reverted, the href value would not be substituted into the path template, preventing any command injection through this vector. The shell command would execute with the literal %u placeholder.
supporting_evidence: Line 142: path = path.replace("%u", href) - direct substitution of external input
Line 145: os.execv("/bin/sh", ["/bin/sh", "-c", path]) - shell command execution
Source summary: href comes from user URLs or temporary file paths
Function calls _fork from _goto (user URLs) and _edit (editor operations)
unresolved_facts: Purpose and security effect of encoder() function on line 143
Whether browser/editor configuration paths are validated before use
Specific validation of href URLs before substitution
review_comment: The code substitutes user-controlled href values directly into shell command templates without proper escaping, creating a command injection vulnerability. When href contains shell metacharacters, they will be interpreted by the shell interpreter. Use shell escaping or parameterization (e.g., shlex.quote()) on href before substitution to neutralize special characters.
